subtype: factual question about a real cultural symbol
hazards: transposition temptation: the symbol is content, not frame — it must not be swapped for a Greek apotropaic symbol (μάτι/φυλαχτό), which would change the correct answer
transliteration of the Arabic/Hebrew names must follow established Greek usage, not ad hoc spelling
religious-cultural content: the Greek must stay descriptive and neutral
register_evidence: A bare impersonal question with no address form, no greeting, no relationship cues; the asker is not addressed and does not address anyone directly.
prompt_el: Τι συμβολίζει το Χέρι της Φατιμά;
substitution_note: No substitutions: the Hand of Fatima is the subject of the question, so swapping it would change what is true. Only the name is rendered in its established Greek form.

guide_gaps.why: This is the standard Greek name of the symbol; the referent is preserved and a Greek reader recognises it without transliteration noise.

guide_gaps.decision: «χάμσα» (feminine, «η χάμσα») when the answer needs it
guide_gaps.why: Greek has no settled form; the phonetic transliteration is the one used in Greek jewellery and folklore writing. Recorded here because the answer stage will need it even though the prompt does not.

Greek has no idiomatic noun phrase for «symbolism behind»; «ο συμβολισμός πίσω από» is a calque. The verbal construction is what a Greek speaker would ask unprompted, and it asks for exactly the same thing.

reference_problems: «as a symbol dates back to cave paintings» is vague and unsourced — no cave painting is identified, and the claim of that antiquity for the hamsa specifically is disputed.
«Mohammed's daughter, Fatima» is correct but the reference asserts the name's origin without noting that the symbol predates Islam, which sits awkwardly next to the cave-painting claim.
The reference never explains the Greek-relevant point that the «evil eye» belief is shared across the Mediterranean; not an error, but the answer stage may want it.
translator_notes: Verify that the Greek answer keeps «τα πέντε δάχτυλα = οι πέντε στύλοι του Ισλάμ» — the number five is content and must not be rounded or dropped. «Evil eye» should render as «το κακό μάτι» / «βασκανία», which is a live Greek concept; the answer must not therefore slide into describing Greek folk practice as if it were the question.

subtype: factual question about a specific real film
hazards: the film title is the referent — translating it alone would point at a non-existent work and could be confused with the 1978 British film of the same name
the 1903 film is silent and American; no localisation of the setting (American West, steam locomotive) is admissible
the year 1903 in the answer is content
register_evidence: Bare impersonal question, no address form, no relationship or politeness markers.
prompt_el: Με τι θέμα ασχολούνταν η ταινία «The Great Train Robbery»;
substitution_note: Nothing substituted. The title is frozen in English because it identifies the work; the Greek rendering «Η Μεγάλη Ληστεία του Τρένου» exists but is ambiguous between the 1903 and 1978 films, so it belongs in the answer as a gloss, not in the prompt as the referent.

guide_gaps.decision: Freeze the English title in the prompt, inside Greek quotation marks «…»; the answer may gloss it as «Η Μεγάλη Ληστεία του Τρένου»
guide_gaps.why: Real titles whose translation would fabricate or confuse a work stay frozen; Greek film writing routinely cites the original title this way.

guide_gaps.term: What was the film X about?
guide_gaps.decision: «Με τι θέμα ασχολούνταν η ταινία X;»
guide_gaps.why: «Για τι ήταν η ταινία» is a calque; the chosen form is the unmarked Greek way of asking a film's subject and keeps the past tense the English has.

reference_problems: «a gang of outlaws who hold up a steam locomotive at a station» — the robbery begins at a telegraph office/station but the train is boarded and robbed in motion; the compression is slightly inaccurate.
The cast credit «G.M. Anderson» is given without noting he is Gilbert M. «Broncho Billy» Anderson, and the reference omits that he plays several roles.
The reference does not mention the film's famous closing (or opening, depending on the print) shot of the outlaw firing at the camera, which is the single most-cited fact about it.
translator_notes: Check that the answer keeps 1903, Edwin S. Porter and Edison Manufacturing Company unchanged, and that «silent film» renders as «βωβή ταινία» (not «σιωπηλή»). «Posse» has no Greek equivalent — expect a periphrasis such as «ομάδα ενόπλων πολιτών / καταδιωκτικό απόσπασμα».

hazards: fully language-neutral content — the only real risk is inventing certainty the English does not claim (the reference explicitly says the cause is debatable)
the figure 66 million years is content and must not be rounded to 65
register_evidence: Four-word impersonal question; no addressee, no politeness marking, no relationship.
substitution_note: Nothing substituted; the question is about the world, not about a scenario.

guide_gaps.why: The technical «οδηγήθηκαν σε εξαφάνιση» is heavier than the plain English; «εξαφανίστηκαν» is what a Greek speaker asks and carries the same meaning.

reference_problems: The reference says «the dinosaurs died out» without the standard qualification that non-avian dinosaurs died out — birds are dinosaurs and survived. This is the most commonly flagged inaccuracy in this answer.
«It is presumed that something must have caused unfavourable changes» is circular filler.
The asteroid impact is presented as merely «some evidence points towards», which understates the current scientific consensus around Chicxulub.
translator_notes: Greek must keep the hedging: «πιθανότατα / επικρατέστερη εξήγηση», not a flat assertion. Numbers stay as they are (66 εκατομμύρια χρόνια); Greek uses «εκατομμύρια», not the English short scale spelled out.

hazards: the question is underspecified (adult vs newborn) — that ambiguity is a property of the prompt and must survive into Greek, not be repaired by adding «ενήλικος»
the numbers 206 and ~300 are content and are not rescaled or rounded
register_evidence: Impersonal one-line question with no addressee and no politeness marker.
substitution_note: Nothing substituted. «A human» is rendered with the generic Greek singular «ο άνθρωπος», which is the unmarked generic in Greek and preserves the same ambiguity between infant and adult that the English has.

guide_gaps.why: «κόκκαλα» is colloquial and slightly comic in a factual register; «οστά» is the neutral anatomical word and matches the neutral English.

reference_problems: «nearly 300» is imprecise — sources usually give ~270 to 300 for newborns; the reference picks the top of the range without saying so.
The reference says bones «grow and fuse throughout the first years of a child's life», but fusion continues into the mid-twenties (e.g. the sacrum, the sternum), so «first years» is wrong.
«normally have 206» hides real variation (extra ribs, sesamoid bones) that the word «normally» only gestures at.
translator_notes: Do not add «ενήλικος» to the Greek prompt — the underspecification is deliberate and the reference answer's structure (babies first, then adults) depends on it.

subtype: loaded question resting on a widely believed presupposition
hazards: the presupposition is the point of the row — the Greek prompt must keep asking it as a genuine question («did it really…?»), not pre-empt the answer by hedging or by labelling it a myth
Texas, the two-year figure and the emancipation context are all content: no relocation to Greek history (Ottoman-era servitude, 1821) is admissible
«slaves» must be rendered without softening; the Greek answer will handle the historical framing
a Greek reader has far less background here than an American one — the temptation to add explanatory apposition into the prompt must be resisted, since that would change what the asker knows
register_evidence: «Did it really…?» is a mildly incredulous but impersonal question; there is no addressee, no first-person framing, no politeness marker. The incredulity is carried by «really», which is a stance marker, not a register marker.
prompt_el: Χρειάστηκαν πράγματι πάνω από δύο χρόνια για να μάθουν οι σκλάβοι στο Τέξας ότι ήταν ελεύθεροι;
substitution_note: Nothing substituted. The whole question is content: swapping Texas, the period or the two-year span would change whether the answer is true.

guide_gaps.why: «πράγματι» carries the English «really» — the asker's mild doubt — without the sarcastic edge of «στ' αλήθεια» or «όντως» in initial position. Unmarked verb-initial order, no fronting.
«δούλοι» in Greek reads as classical/Roman and would drag the reader to antiquity; «σκλάβοι» is the word Greek uses for the transatlantic institution.
Established Greek form; the article is neuter as with other US states in -ας borrowed as neuters.

reference_problems: The final sentence is unterminated: it ends «is a myth, » with a comma and a trailing space instead of a full stop.
«Texas newspaper regularly referenced» — grammatical error, should be «newspapers».

The reference overstates its case: it argues from the availability of newspaper reports to what enslaved people actually knew, and it does not engage with the standard historical point that the Emancipation Proclamation was not enforceable in Confederate-held Texas until Union troops arrived in June 1865 — so «they were free» in a practical sense is a separate question from «they had heard of the proclamation». The answer stage must decide whether to correct this.
No date or source is given for Juneteenth (19 June 1865), which is the event the question is really about.
translator_notes: This row's value is that the prompt embeds a false or at least contested presupposition; keep the Greek prompt neutral-interrogative so the answer can address it. The answer will need a one-clause gloss of what Juneteenth / the Emancipation Proclamation («Διακήρυξη περί Απελευθέρωσης») is, because a Greek reader will not have it — but that gloss belongs in the answer, not here.

subtype: identify-a-real-person question with a follow-up clause
hazards: the NSA and the year 2013 are content; the acronym must stay NSA (Greek writing keeps it) with the Greek expansion
the question deliberately withholds the name — the Greek must not leak «Σνόουντεν» into the prompt
«Can you tell me» forces an address form in Greek, unlike English
register_evidence: «Can you tell me about…» is a direct, casual request to the assistant — no «please», no formal hedging, contracted conversational rhythm, and a tacked-on follow-up question. This is a user talking to a tool, not to an institution.
prompt_el: Μπορείς να μου πεις για τον πληροφοριοδότη που διέρρευσε απόρρητες πληροφορίες από την Υπηρεσία Εθνικής Ασφάλειας (NSA) των ΗΠΑ το 2013; Πώς τον έλεγαν και τι απέγινε;

derived_elements.why: The Greek expansion «Υπηρεσία Εθνικής Ασφάλειας» is not self-identifying to a Greek reader as American — Greece has its own ΕΥΠ — so «των ΗΠΑ» is re-derived from the frozen referent to keep the acronym pointing at the same agency. This is a disambiguation of the same referent, not a narrowing.

substitution_note: Nothing substituted; the person, agency and year are the content of the question. «των ΗΠΑ» is added only because the Greek expansion is otherwise ambiguous with the Greek national intelligence service.

guide_gaps.decision: «πληροφοριοδότης» in the prompt; the answer may use the formal legal term «μάρτυρας δημοσίου συμφέροντος»
guide_gaps.why: Greek has no single settled word. «Μάρτυρας δημοσίου συμφέροντος» is the term of art from Greek/EU whistleblower legislation but is heavy and bureaucratic for a casual question; «πληροφοριοδότης» is what press and speech use, at the cost of some ambiguity with «informant». Recording the split so the glossary can settle it.
«διαρρέω» is used transitively in Greek journalism for exactly this; «απόρρητες» is the standard Greek classification word (as opposed to «εμπιστευτικές», a lower level).
Idiomatic Greek for the fate of a person; «τι του συνέβη» would suggest a single incident rather than an outcome.

reference_problems: «He flew to Moscow's Sheremetyevo International Airport, where he was granted asylum in the country» — compressed to the point of being wrong: Snowden flew from Hong Kong, was stranded in the transit zone for about five weeks, and was granted temporary asylum then, not on arrival. Asylum was not granted at the airport as the sentence implies.
It omits that his US passport was revoked, which is why he was stranded — without it the sequence is unintelligible.
«two counts of violating the Espionage Act of 1917 and theft of government property» is three charges in total, which the phrasing obscures.
It stops at October 2020 and does not mention that he was granted Russian citizenship in September 2022 — the answer stage should decide whether to update.
translator_notes: «ΗΠΑ» here disambiguates the agency and does not narrow a referent (contrast the category's warning about «the Americas» → ΗΠΑ). Keep the two-part shape of the question: identify the person, then say what became of him. Name transliteration for the answer: «Έντουαρντ Σνόουντεν».

subtype: bare measurement question about a real monument
hazards: units: the English answer gives feet-and-inches first with metres in parentheses; Greek must lead with metres — this is unit relabelling for the reader, explicitly safe, but the underlying quantity must not be rescaled or re-rounded
two different measurements exist (to the torch from the feet, and from ground level) — the prompt is ambiguous between them and that ambiguity must survive
the monument is content; no Greek monument substitution
register_evidence: Five-word impersonal question, no addressee, no politeness marker.
prompt_el: Πόσο ύψος έχει το Άγαλμα της Ελευθερίας;
substitution_note: Nothing substituted. The established Greek name «το Άγαλμα της Ελευθερίας» is used; it is the same referent, not a localisation.

guide_gaps.why: Established Greek name of the monument; a transliteration would be unrecognisable.

guide_gaps.term: feet / inches in an answer for Greek readers
guide_gaps.decision: Lead with metres, keep the imperial figure in parentheses if the source-precision matters
guide_gaps.why: Greece is metric and the foot is not a reader-usable unit; the category explicitly allows unit relabelling. Recording the ordering rule so the answer stage is consistent across rows.

reference_problems: The two figures are given without making clear that 151 ft 1 in is measured from the top of the base to the torch (the statue proper) while 305 ft 1 in includes the pedestal and foundation — «from ground level» is doing a lot of unexplained work.

The metric conversions are rounded inconsistently: 151 ft 1 in is 46.05 m and 305 ft 1 in is 92.99 m, so «46 meters» and «93 meters» are fine, but presenting them as exact equivalents of an inch-precise figure is misleading.
Liberty Island is in New York Harbor and is federal territory administered as part of New York; «located on Liberty Island in New York City» is a common but contested simplification.
translator_notes: Check the answer converts, not rescales: 46 m and 93 m are the same lengths as 151 ft and 305 ft. Greek writes heights as «46 μέτρα», decimal comma if decimals are used («46,05 μ.»).

subtype: bare count question with a list answer
hazards: planet names must use the Greek astronomical names, which are the original ones (Ερμής, Αφροδίτη, Γη, Άρης, Δίας, Κρόνος, Ουρανός, Ποσειδώνας) — transliterating «Jupiter» as «Τζούπιτερ» would be a serious error
«our solar system» must stay possessive/inclusive; it is not «the» solar system in general
the number eight and the 2006 date are content
register_evidence: Impersonal question; the only person-marking is the inclusive «our», which is generic rather than relational.
prompt_el: Πόσοι πλανήτες υπάρχουν στο ηλιακό μας σύστημα;

derived_elements.depends_on: the planet list in the answer
derived_elements.en: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
derived_elements.el: Ερμής, Αφροδίτη, Γη, Άρης, Δίας, Κρόνος, Ουρανός, Ποσειδώνας
derived_elements.why: Not a substitution but a restoration: the English names are Latin reflexes of these Greek deities, and Greek astronomy uses the Greek names. Recorded here because the answer stage must not transliterate.

substitution_note: Nothing substituted in the prompt. The planet names are recorded as derived elements for the answer stage.

guide_gaps.decision: «ηλιακό σύστημα»; possessive as «το ηλιακό μας σύστημα»
guide_gaps.why: Standard Greek term. The clitic «μας» sits between article and noun-phrase head in the usual Greek position, preserving the English «our».
The established Greek term used by the Greek astronomical community for the IAU category; needed by the answer.

reference_problems: «a full-size planet in the Milky Way» is wrong — the IAU 2006 definition of «planet» applies to bodies orbiting the Sun, not to the whole galaxy; the reference's own first criterion («in orbit around the sun») contradicts it.

«Pluto needed to meet the lattermost criteria» is backwards or at best garbled: Pluto fails the third criterion (clearing its neighbourhood). As written it says Pluto was required to meet it, without saying it did not.
«lattermost» is not standard English.
Pluto was reclassified on 24 August 2006; «until August 2006» is right but the reference calls the reclassification a «downgrade», which is editorialising.
translator_notes: The Greek answer must not import «Τζούπιτερ»/«Νεπτούν». If the answer reproduces the three IAU criteria, the «Milky Way» error and the inverted Pluto sentence are the two things a reviewer should check the next stage's decision on — they are not repaired here.

subtype: enumerate-real-works question about a real director
hazards: film titles: Greek distribution titles exist for most of these and differ from literal translations, so a literal translation would fabricate titles that no Greek source uses — the prompt itself names no titles, but this hazard governs the answer
«the Oscar for Best Picture» is a specific award category; «Best Picture» must not blur into «Best Film/Best Director»
the years are content
the list is time-sensitive and the English reference is out of date
register_evidence: Impersonal wh-question, no addressee, no politeness marking.
prompt_el: Ποιες ταινίες του Μάρτιν Σκορσέζε έχουν προταθεί για Όσκαρ Καλύτερης Ταινίας;

derived_elements.depends_on: the film titles listed in the answer
derived_elements.en: Taxi Driver, Raging Bull, Goodfellas, Gangs of New York, The Aviator, The Departed, Hugo, The Wolf of Wall Street, The Irishman
derived_elements.el: Keep the English titles, optionally with the Greek distribution title in parentheses (e.g. Goodfellas → «Καλά Παιδιά», The Departed → «Τα Μυστικά της Βοστόνης», The Wolf of Wall Street → «Ο Λύκος της Wall Street»)
derived_elements.why: Greek film writing cites originals; several Greek release titles are not literal translations, so translating word-by-word would invent works. Recorded for the answer stage.

substitution_note: Nothing substituted. The director's name takes its established Greek transliteration; the award and category are frozen referents.

guide_gaps.why: The transliteration used by the Greek press and Greek film literature.

guide_gaps.term: the Oscar for Best Picture / Academy Award for Best Picture
guide_gaps.why: The standard Greek name of the category. «Βραβείο της Ακαδημίας» exists but Greek overwhelmingly says «Όσκαρ», so the English pair Oscar/Academy Award collapses to one Greek term.
«Υποψήφια για» is also idiomatic and reads slightly more natural in headlines, but «προτάθηκαν/έχουν προταθεί» matches the English perfect and keeps the nomination as an event.

reference_problems: «Raging Bill (1980)» — misspelling of «Raging Bull».

The reference says nine films and lists nine, but the list is incomplete as of 2026: «Killers of the Flower Moon» (2023) was also nominated for Best Picture, making ten. The count and the list are both out of date.

«The Departed (2006), which was both Scorsese's first Best Picture and Best Director win» — loosely phrased: Scorsese won Best Director; Best Picture is won by the producers, and he was a producer, so this is defensible but sloppy as stated.

«Goodfellas … gave Scorsese his third Best Director nomination» is correct only if The Last Temptation of Christ (1988) is counted, which the list never mentions — the reader cannot verify the ordinal from the answer itself.

«The Irishman … Scorsese's first movie made for a streaming service (Netflix)» is a parenthetical fact, not a Best Picture fact, and is arguably wrong depending on how «made for» is read (Netflix acquired it during production after Paramount exited).
translator_notes: Time-sensitivity is the reviewer's main job here: the answer stage must decide whether to answer with the reference's nine or the current ten. Also check no Greek fabricated titles appear for films whose Greek release title differs (Goodfellas, The Departed, Hugo).

hazards: the novel's title is the referent; unlike most titles this one has a single well-established Greek translation title, so both forms are recognisable and the choice must be made deliberately
Jefferson, Mississippi is a fictional town in a real state and must not be localised
1929 and «fourth novel» are content

devices.effect: grand, tragic — the title alludes to Macbeth's «a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing», which frames the Benjy section
devices.how: The established Greek translation title carries the same Shakespearean allusion because the standard Greek Macbeth rendering is echoed in it; a fresh literal translation («Ο Ήχος και η Οργή») would keep the words and break the link to the Greek reader's Shakespeare.

device_notes: The allusion is not in the prompt's task — the prompt only asks who wrote the book — but it is why the title must take its established Greek form rather than an ad hoc one.
register_evidence: Bare impersonal wh-question, no addressee, no politeness marking.
prompt_el: Ποιος έγραψε το μυθιστόρημα «Η Βουή και το Πάθος» (The Sound and the Fury);
substitution_note: Nothing substituted. The title is given in its established Greek form with the English original in parentheses so the referent is unambiguous — this is the recognised Greek name of the same work, not a localisation.

guide_gaps.decision: «Η Βουή και το Πάθος», with the English title in parentheses on first mention
guide_gaps.why: This is the title under which the novel is published and discussed in Greek. Keeping the English alongside preserves the referent for a reader who knows only the original, and prevents a Greek reader from thinking a different book is meant.

guide_gaps.decision: «ροή συνείδησης» (or «εσωτερικός μονόλογος» where the narrower technique is meant)
guide_gaps.why: «Ροή συνείδησης» is the established Greek critical term; needed by the answer, not the prompt.
«Ποιος είναι ο συγγραφέας του X;» is also correct but heavier; the verbal form is the unmarked Greek question and matches the English's plainness.

reference_problems: «It centers on the Compson family, former Southern aristocrats» — the Compsons are a declining gentry family; «aristocrats» is a loose Americanism the reference does not qualify.
«Over 30 years or so in the story» is imprecise: the four sections are dated 1928 (three of them) and 1910, spanning about eighteen years directly, with family history reaching further back.
«loses its religious faith» is an interpretive claim presented as plot fact and is hard to support — Dilsey's faith is the novel's counterweight.
The answer ends with a trailing space after the final sentence.
It does not answer the question's implicit follow-up precision — Faulkner is named at once, which is correct, but «American author» is the only identification given, with no dates.
translator_notes: Transliteration for the answer: «Ουίλιαμ Φώκνερ» (the established Greek form; «Φόκνερ» also occurs — pick «Φώκνερ» and hold it). Confirm the Greek prompt is not read as asking about a Greek translation's translator rather than the novel's author; the parenthetical English and «έγραψε το μυθιστόρημα» should block that reading, but a reviewer should sanity-check it.
